q-152363.name: Question 1
q-152363.worked_solution:
The square root of a quotient of two positive numbers is equal to the quotient of the square roots of the numbers. Therefore, 

$$
\sqrt{\frac{49}{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{49}}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{7}{\sqrt{3}}
$$

A quotient of square roots of two positive numbers is equal to the square root of the quotient of the numbers. Therefore,

$$
\frac{\sqrt{32}}{\sqrt{18}}=\sqrt{\frac{32}{18}}=\sqrt{\frac{16}{9}}=\sqrt{{(\frac{4}{3})}^{2}}=\frac{4}{3}
$$

q-99612.name: Question 8
q-99612.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the fraction under the radical as follows:

$$
\sqrt[3]{-\frac{216}{343}}=\sqrt[3]{\frac{(-216)}{343}}
$$

The cube root of a quotient of two numbers is equal to the quotient of the cube roots of the numbers. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{\frac{(-216)}{343}} & =\frac{\sqrt[3]{-216}}{\sqrt[3]{343}} \\  & =\frac{-6}{7} \\  & =-\frac{6}{7}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we rewrite the fraction under the radical as follows:

(−216)3433=−21633433=−67=−67.
